description: PRD-120: Skills Marketplace & Agent Catalog — Import ~65 professional agent skills from agency-agents, build agent templates marketplace with one-click deploy, and create the Business Plan Mission Template that configures entire workspaces.

userStories.title: Create skill directory structure and import conversion script
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a directory structure for skills and a Python script that converts agency-agents markdown files to Automatos SKILL.md format.
acceptanceCriteria: Create automatos-skills/skills/ directory with subdirectories: engineering, design, marketing, sales, product, project-management, testing, support, paid-media, specialized

Create automatos-skills/README.md with skill format specification (frontmatter: name, version, category, tags, description, recommended_tools, recommended_model + sections: Identity, Core Mission, Workflow, Deliverables, Rules)

Create scripts/import_agency_skills.py that: reads a source markdown file with YAML frontmatter, extracts name/description/tools/services, maps tools to Automatos equivalents (workspace_read_file, workspace_write_file, workspace_exec, composio tools), assigns recommended_model based on complexity, strips platform-specific references, outputs Automatos SKILL.md format
Script accepts --source-dir (agency-agents clone path) and --output-dir (automatos-skills/skills/) arguments
Script has --category flag to process one category at a time
Script has --dry-run flag that prints conversion plan without writing files
Script maps agency-agents divisions to Automatos categories (engineering->engineering, design->design, marketing->marketing, etc.)
Script trims output to 200-400 lines per skill, removing filler and emoji section markers
Run script with --dry-run on at least one sample file to verify output format
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The script should use standard library only (no extra deps). Tool mapping: agency-agents uses generic tool names like 'WebFetch', 'Read', 'Write', 'Edit', 'Bash' — map these to workspace_read_file, workspace_write_file, workspace_exec. Services like 'GitHub' map to GITHUB composio tool. Model mapping: simple/repetitive tasks -> haiku-4.5, standard work -> sonnet-4.6, complex reasoning -> opus-4.6. The script parses YAML frontmatter between --- delimiters.

No output file references OpenClaw, Cursor, Qwen, or other non-Automatos platforms
All recommended_tools reference valid Automatos tool names (workspace_*, composio tools like GITHUB, SLACK, GOOGLE_SHEETS)
At least 18 SKILL.md files created in automatos-skills/skills/engineering/ and automatos-skills/skills/design/

userStories.notes: Clone to scripts/vendor/agency-agents (gitignored). The agency-agents repo structure has divisions as top-level directories with agent markdown files inside. If the import script needs tweaks for edge cases in the source files, fix the script.

userStories.title: Add agent_catalog_templates DB table and migration
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a database table to store agent templates for the marketplace one-click deploy feature.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Alembic migration that adds agent_catalog_templates table with columns: id (PK), slug (VARCHAR unique), name (VARCHAR), category (VARCHAR), description (TEXT), persona (TEXT), skill_slug (VARCHAR — references skill directory slug), recommended_model (VARCHAR), recommended_tools (JSON array), tags (JSON array), icon (VARCHAR(10)), tier (VARCHAR default 'free'), is_active (BOOLEAN default true), created_at (TIMESTAMP), updated_at (TIMESTAMP)
Add workspace_id (INTEGER, nullable, FK to workspaces.id) for future per-workspace templates, default NULL = global
Add AgentCatalogTemplate SQLAlchemy model in orchestrator/core/models/core.py
Add relationship to Workspace model if workspace_id FK is present
Migration runs successfully (alembic upgrade head)
Existing tests still pass — no behavioral changes yet, schema only
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Migration goes in orchestrator/alembic/versions/. Use revision naming like prd120_agent_catalog_templates. The existing AgentTemplate in core.py (line ~863) is a Pydantic BaseModel used for the creation wizard — do NOT modify it. Create a new SQLAlchemy model AgentCatalogTemplate. Follow existing migration patterns (see alembic/versions/ for examples). The slug should match the skill directory name (e.g. 'growth-hacker' matches automatos-skills/skills/marketing/growth-hacker/).

userStories.title: Seed agent catalog templates from imported skills
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to populate the agent_catalog_templates table with entries for all imported skills.
acceptanceCriteria: Create scripts/seed_agent_catalog.py that reads all SKILL.md files from automatos-skills/skills/
Script parses frontmatter (name, category, tags, description, recommended_tools, recommended_model) from each SKILL.md
Script generates a persona field from the Identity section of each SKILL.md

Script assigns icon based on category (engineering=gear, design=palette, marketing=chart, sales=money, product=target, pm=clipboard, support=building, testing=magnifier, paid-media=megaphone, specialized=star)
Script creates INSERT statements or uses SQLAlchemy to upsert into agent_catalog_templates
Script is idempotent — running twice doesn't create duplicates (upsert on slug)
Also create an Alembic data migration that calls the seed logic so it runs on deploy
After running seed, agent_catalog_templates has 55+ rows
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The seed script should be runnable standalone (python scripts/seed_agent_catalog.py) AND as an Alembic migration. Use the frontmatter parser from the import script (or a simple YAML parser). For persona generation, extract the Identity section content and prefix with 'You are a...'. The recommended_model should map to actual model IDs: haiku-4.5 -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, sonnet-4.6 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6, opus-4.6 -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6. Use config.py for model IDs if they exist there.

userStories.title: Business Plan mission template configuration
userStories.description: As a platform developer, I want a Business Plan mission template that decomposes into research, document generation, and workspace configuration phases.
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'business_plan' template to orchestrator/modules/coordination/templates.py TEMPLATE_REGISTRY

Template has 4 phases with parallel groups: Phase 1 (research — 3 parallel tasks: market research, competitive analysis, financial modeling), Phase 2 (document generation — sequential: exec summary, market analysis, financial projections, synthesis into full doc), Phase 3 (workspace config — 3 parallel tasks: create agents from catalog, create playbooks, create board tasks), Phase 4 (verification — summary report)
Template match keywords: 'business plan', 'startup', 'business idea', 'launch a business', 'start a company'
Template has required_input fields: business_name, business_type, industry (required) + target_market, budget_range, goals (optional)
Template tasks use agent roles from _ROLE_SYNONYMS: researcher, analyst, writer, admin/operations
Phase 3 workspace config tasks reference platform tools: platform_create_agent, platform_install_skill, platform_create_playbook, platform_configure_heartbeat, platform_create_board_task
Template includes synthesis tasks after parallel convergences (Phase 1 -> synthesis -> Phase 2)
Estimated token budget: 500000 (from PRD)
Template renders correctly via render_template() — returns valid task list with dependencies
WIRING TEST: match_template('Write a business plan for my coffee brand') returns business_plan template
WIRING TEST: render_template for business_plan has parallel groups in Phase 1 and Phase 3
Typecheck passes
All tests pass
userStories.notes: Follow the exact same pattern as existing templates (research_and_report, content_pipeline, etc.) in templates.py. TaskTemplate dataclass has: title, agent_role, task_type, description, sequence, complexity, parallel_group, depends_on. Use the parallel group patterns from PRD-82C (already implemented). Phase 3 tasks are unique — they use platform tools to configure the workspace. The admin/operations role needs to be in _ROLE_SYNONYMS in agent_matcher.py — check and add if missing. Template rendering was updated in US-006 of PRD-82C to support explicit depends_on.
